The **AHA-studiet** (the AHA study) is a mortality-reducing clinical study focused on acute abdominal surgery that serves as a foundational piece of evidence for the Danish healthcare system's quality improvement initiatives [^src1]. Frequently referenced in the Akut Kirurgi Databasen (AKDB) reports under the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), the study underpins several national quality indicators aimed at standardizing and improving acute surgical care.

The study's primary significance lies in its documentation of the effects of anesthesiological preoperative optimization. Patients in the AHA study were optimized in the Intensive Care Unit (IMA), Intermediate Care Unit (ITA), or directly in the operating room immediately after the decision to operate was made [^src1]. This specific practice forms the evidence base for the clinical recommendations associated with [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]], which tracks preoperative optimization [^src1]. 

Furthermore, the AHA study has contributed to broader clinical guidelines beyond preoperative optimization. In conjunction with the ELPQUICK study, it highlighted that early antibiotic treatment is a key initiative in lowering mortality for acute abdominal surgery, thereby supporting the evidence for [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] [^src2]. The study also incorporated the standard use of [[epidural|epidural]] analgesia for high-risk abdominal patients, a practice that contributed to the overall reduction in mortality observed in the trial [^src3]. 

## Mentions

- **Page 21**: "I det mortalitets-sænkende AHA-studie, blev patienterne optimeret på IMA / ITA / eller på operationsgangen forud for operation umiddelbart efter det var besluttet at patienten skulle opereres." [^src1]
- **Page 11**: "I AHA og ELPQUICK studierne, der begge har forbedret mortalitet, er tidlig antibiotikabehandling et af de tiltag, der har været med til at sænke mortaliteten på akut abdominal kirurgi." [^src2]
- **Page 46**: "Standard brug af epidural til abdominal høj risikopatienter var en del af AHA studiet som overordnet set nedbragte mortaliteten." [^src3]
